text: 🇲🇽🔍 Twelve years on, the state keeps digging for Ayotzinapa's 43. "Before September 26 — twelve years since the disappearance — the FGR may present a public report on new lines of investigation." — Claudia Sheinbaum, after meeting the families, Aug 27 Sheinbaum met the parents of the 43 at Palacio Nacional to brief them on new leads, recent arrests and phone-record analysis. One line touches former Guerrero governor Ángel Aguirre. No case buried; the search continues.

🇲🇽✊ Angela Davis at UNAM: "an institution in the defense of civil rights." "Angela Davis is an institution in the defense of women's rights and civil rights — a woman who has fought her whole life for freedom." She quotes Davis: "What is feminism? Considering a woman a person." — Claudia Sheinbaum, on Davis's UNAM visit, Aug 27 Davis packed UNAM on Aug 26 for the dialogue "Abolition, Feminism, Now!" with Gina Dent and Amneris Chaparro.

🔥🇲🇽 Mexico recovers over $5 million from García Luna's network. "More than five million dollars tied to the Genaro García Luna case — recovered by the state." — Sheinbaum administration, announced Aug 27 The Financial Intelligence Unit traced the funds to the Weinberg family network. García Luna — Calderón's security chief — was convicted in a New York federal court of taking cartel bribes. UIF chief Omar Reyes Colmenares details the recovery Friday.

🚨🇲🇽 "A governor with dual nationality has two interests." "When you hold dual nationality, a governor has two interests. The nation's interest must stand above any other interest of any other State or nation in the world." — Claudia Sheinbaum, on blocking foreign interference, Aug 27 The reform bars would-be presidents and governors from holding a second passport, invoking a foreign nationality, or seeking another country's diplomatic protection — a firewall against injerencia extranjera in Mexican public office.

🇲🇽⚖️ Only Mexicans — with no second passport — may lead Mexico. "Every Mexican who wishes to be president, governor or head of government must be only Mexican — hold no other nationality, nor have acquired one." — Claudia Sheinbaum, presenting the reform, Aug 27 Sheinbaum sent Congress a constitutional reform (Articles 82, 116, 122): candidates for president, governor and head of government must renounce any other nationality before registering, and may not invoke a foreign passport or another state's protection in office.

🏭🇲🇽 <u>MEXICO EXPORTS LIKE NEVER BEFORE</u>

Mexican exports hit an all-time record $81.4 billion in July, up 43.7% year-on-year, with manufacturing up 45.7% and electrical/electronic goods soaring 134%, INEGI reported. Non-oil exports to the US jumped 49.8%. Mexico's January–July trade surplus now stands at $9.26 billion — nearly eight times the $1.18 billion booked in the same period of 2025.

✊🇲🇽 <u>ANGELA DAVIS AT UNAM: DESPAIR IS NOT AN OPTION</u>

Over 2,000 people packed UNAM's Centro Cultural Universitario to hear Angela Davis: "Despair is not an option," she told the overflowing hall, calling the "primary task of radical activists" the generation of hope against rising fascism. Davis and Gina Dent closed the night with a statement of solidarity for Palestine — in the heart of Latin America's largest public university.

🇲🇽🇵🇸 <u>MEXICO CITY STANDS WITH PALESTINE</u>

This Saturday, Aug 30, Mexican collectives fill Mexico City's Teatro del Pueblo for "Palestine: Genocide, Apartheid and Resistance," hosting Jamal Juma' of the BDS National Committee and BDS Latin America coordinator Germán Romano. The aim, organizers say, is to "denounce the formal structures of discrimination and dispossession." Brigada Sumud and allied groups open the day with the Coro La Coraza choir.

🌽🇲🇽 <u>MAYA COMMUNITIES WIN: PROBE THE GLYPHOSATE IN OUR WATER</u>

Mexico's Supreme Court unanimously sided with 17 Maya communities in Hopelchén, Campeche, ordering SEMARNAT, CONAGUA and COFEPRIS to investigate glyphosate contamination in their water. The court set a precautionary standard rooted in Indigenous rights: "the State cannot wait for absolute scientific certainty about possible environmental damage before beginning prevention." The communities first sued back in 2020.

text:
🔥🇲🇽 <u>THE COURT TO THE OPPOSITION: YOU'RE NOT MEXICO</u>

Mexico's electoral court (TEPJF) ordered the new right-wing party "Somos México" to drop its name, logo and colors by Aug 31, ruling that claiming to be Mexico amounts to a "symbolic appropriation of national identity" — no single faction gets to brand itself as the whole nation. The party says it will comply "under protest," calling it an "outrage." Sheinbaum backed the ruling: a party is not the country.
